Are AI assistants making us faster, or just making us rusty?

A recent discussion pointed out that AI isn't simply replacing engineering roles, it risks deskilling them if we stop understanding the fundamentals.

When AI writes code or logs alerts, it is easy to become a passive spectator. But when production breaks, automated suggestions cannot replace real debugging intuition.

Here is a 3-step study roadmap to protect your technical depth:

1. Deep dive into system fundamentals. Understand OS concepts, networking, and database locks before relying on automated helpers.

2. Debug by hand first. Spend 15 minutes tracing stack traces and logs independently before asking an AI tool for the solution.

3. Build small services from scratch. Write real APIs and deploy them yourself so you know every failure point.

Use AI to speed up boilerplate, not to outsource your critical thinking.

How do you ensure you are still building real problem-solving skills while using AI tools?
